messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] singular matricex using cim()
messages.body_plain:
There are probably multiple markers with identical genotypes, and
the forward selection algorithm in cim() [which is rather roughly
implemented] is getting singularities.

You might try first running calc.genoprob with error.prob=0.01 or
=0.001.
That would allow a bit of fuzziness and might prevent this problem.

karl

messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] Re: how to tell scantwo which scanone to use for
messages.body_plain:
R/qtl (available at http://www.rqtl.org) uses classical methods.
For Bayesian multiple QTL mapping, consider the R/qtlbim package
(available at http://www.qtlbim.org).

The R/qtlbim package is distinct from R/qtl, but some of the same data
formats, and relies on R/qtl for some things (such as data import).

regards,
karl

messages.body_plain:
Hi - I've got a small problem with scantwo permutation.  I've run 800
permutes in batches of 100 permutes each, one batch per processor on a
dual processor quad-core using eight separate loads of R (from the
same .RData file).  The problem is that I'm not sure how to combine
each permute batch with each other to have a totalled file of 800
permutes from which I can get the proper threshold for significance at
a=0.05.  The individual loads of R don't seem to recognize each
other's work, even when I "save.image", and so I can't seem to combine
them with the array joining

allperm <- c(perm1,perm2....perm8)

I've tried writing them to disk (write(perm1,file="outperm1",sep=",")
and reloading them with 'load("perm1")' but it gives the following
error:

Error: bad restore file magic number (file may be corrupted) -- no
data loaded
In addition: Warning message:
file 'perm1' has magic number ''
   Use of save versions prior to 2 is deprecated

I'm trying to figure out how to proceed but so far no luck.  Are
people using multiple processors for this kind of work, and, if so, do
I need some kind of third-party program to control connectivity among
the multiple invocations of R?

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Extracting scantwo results
messages.body_plain:
I often split permutations across multiple processors.
You need to be sure to set the seed for the random number generator,
differently for each run.  I generally use some large number,
say 27005771, and then use set.seed(27005771+1), set.seed(27005771+2),
etc.
in the individual runs.

You then need to save the results from each run to separate files,
and later load them and combine them.

   save(perm1, file="perm1.RData")
   save(perm2, file="perm2.RData")
   etc.

   load(perm1)
   load(perm2)
   etc.

   perm <- c(perm1, perm2, ....)

The problems you're having seem to do with save and load and not with
c.scantwoperm().

karl
